rationale: Correct Gemini Solar + Storage to the current 51%/49% ownership structure confirmed during the project's February 2026 refinancing: Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP owns 51% and APG owns 49% on behalf of ABP. The April 2024 Valley of Fire transaction was a Quinbrook-managed fund continuation rather than an exit by Quinbrook, while Blackstone Strategic Partners and Ares Management Infrastructure Secondaries participated as fund investors and are not direct Gemini owners. Replace the unsupported project founding claim and duplicate transaction milestones with the documented Quinbrook acquisition, federal approval, APG investment, continuation-fund acquisition, and commercial-operations milestones. Also add the official project website, use the asset's Clark County location, disclose both stakes and vehicles, refresh the operating description, and set the verification date. Current Quinbrook, Primergy, APG, and 2026 refinancing sources show no subsequent sale or pending ownership change.

beforeImage.name: Gemini Solar + Storage
beforeImage.description: Gemini is a utility-scale solar and battery storage project located in Clark County, Nevada. Its customer base is the Nevada power market and contracted offtakers that purchase output and capacity from one of the largest co-located solar-plus-storage assets in the country. The project follows an asset-heavy contracted operating model centered on long-lived generation and storage infrastructure. Public disclosures describe approximately 690 megawatts of solar capacity paired with 380 megawatts of battery storage, with the project representing one of the largest solar-plus-storage installations in the United States. The asset reached full commercial operations in 2024 after construction and financing by Quinbrook and Primergy. APG acquired a 49% interest on behalf of ABP in 2022, and Quinbrook's Valley of Fire fund acquired the remaining 51% in 2024.

afterImage.name: Gemini Solar + Storage
afterImage.description: Gemini Solar + Storage is an operating 690 MWac solar photovoltaic and 380 MW / approximately 1,416 MWh battery storage project in Clark County, Nevada, developed by Quinbrook with its portfolio company Primergy. The co-located facility supplies NV Energy under a 25-year power purchase agreement and is designed to meet approximately 10% of Nevada's peak power demand. APG acquired a 49% interest on behalf of ABP in 2022. In April 2024, Quinbrook's Valley of Fire Continuation Fund LP acquired the remaining 51%, and the project reached full commercial operations in 2024. A February 2026 refinancing continued to identify the same 51% Quinbrook / 49% APG ownership structure.
